tasks.short: Arrange exhibit construction with outside contractors

steps.what: Arrange contractors, resolving exhibit scope, capability, site access, price and construction commitments

tasks.design: Keep contractor arrangement with the designer, using {PROJECT} and {EMAIL} to record agreements. The designer checks the exact scope and commitments before confirming them.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contractor availability and willingness to deliver the proposed construction require direct agreement.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing project records can support the coordination without a new allocation service.
tasks.still_hard: Resolving practical scope, capability, access restrictions and changed construction conditions.
tasks.human_edge: The designer negotiates a workable commitment and recognises when specialist advice is required.

reach.task: Explain capability, availability and proposed methods
reach.learn: Which design details prevent a firm commitment

evidence.claim: Arranging site-specific construction depends on negotiation and practical scope assessment; a time saving is not established.

assumptions: Boundary is arranging construction, not writing the underlying exhibit design or performing construction.
Contractors supply proposals and availability during s1; the designer checks and records them in the same counted time. No structured suitability or availability flags are assumed.
Use existing project records before adding procurement automation.
No incremental upkeep is added because this retains the current human arrangement process.
research_questions: How much arrangement effort is negotiation versus repeated clerical copying?

already_counted.description: Scope discussion, commitment checking and confirmation

approvals.approved_version: Exact contractor, construction scope, price, dates, access conditions and responsibilities; any change requires renewed review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; zero gross and net saving. No separate document-production baseline is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Coordinate removal of sets, props and exhibits with crews and venue staff

tasks.design: Keep removal coordination with the designer and crews. Use {PROJECT} to record the sequence and item destinations during the coordination.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual site readiness, item ownership and crew dependencies must be resolved on the day.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing project notes can hold the shared sequence without a new scheduling system.
tasks.still_hard: Adapting removal when crews, borrowed items or venue conditions change.
tasks.human_edge: The designer settles priorities and checks that the people involved understand the plan.
tasks.altitude: Return the venue and exhibit items in an agreed sequence.

reach.learn: Which removal activities depend on venue readiness

evidence.claim: Live removal coordination is situational work; a scheduling tool alone does not remove its labour.

assumptions: Boundary is coordination, not physically carrying or dismantling items.
Venue staff confirm event completion and access during s1; the designer verifies item destinations and crew dependencies in that counted time. No free readiness signal is assumed.
No incremental upkeep is proposed because no new dispatch automation is introduced.
unknowns: How destinations and ownership are recorded
research_questions: Are delays caused by missing destination information or physical access constraints?

already_counted.description: Readiness checks and live removal coordination

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; zero gross and net saving. No unobserved recurring dispatch baseline is assumed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Provide promotional and supporting exhibit materials

steps.what: Collect verified exhibit facts, permitted assets and specifications for supportive materials
Draft and check exhibit notices, brochures, invitations and publicity copy

loop.purpose: Adapt verified exhibit information for different supporting materials
loop.input: Verified content packet and requested audiences from s1
loop.output: Source-linked copy drafts for the requested materials
loop.check: Designer checks factual claims, dates, names, permissions and audience meaning
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unanswered facts stay blank for manual resolution
loop.why_not_simpler: Audience-specific explanatory copy needs interpretation beyond field substitution

steps.what: Populate defined print and digital templates from checked copy and mapped assets
Proof supportive materials, resolve questions and provide the exact approved versions

tasks.design: Draft source-checked copy in {DOCS}, then populate fixed templates in {OTHER}, a visual layout editor. The designer proofs each output before providing it through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same exhibit facts are rewritten and placed into several supporting formats.
tasks.enabler_now: Figma Buzz supports locked templates and spreadsheet-driven variants [S3]; reviewed copy drafting is a separate E1 design proposal.
tasks.still_hard: Audience fit, reliable exhibit facts, image permissions and the final visual proof.
tasks.human_edge: The designer decides what the audience needs and owns the released material.

ambition.what: Offer a reviewed plain-language handout when the organiser identifies an audience need.

tasks.altitude: Manage one checked information source across supporting formats.

reach.task: Verify event facts and distribution needs
reach.learn: Which supporting formats reach the intended audience

evidence.claim: Figma Buzz supports locked templates and spreadsheet-driven content variants.
Reviewed audience-specific copy drafting and the saving range are unmeasured design scenarios.

assumptions: Boundary includes producing and providing the requested supporting materials, not running an advertising campaign.

Event organiser supplies names, dates, access details and permitted assets; designer verifies and captures them in s1 with template dimensions, asset identifiers and field mapping. Designer produces checked copy in s2. Those exact fields feed s3; missing fields or overflow stop for manual repair in s4.
Use native template variants before building a custom generator.
Any extra plain-language handout is additional service and its production time is excluded from savings.
unknowns: How many materials reuse the same facts
Whether template population is already automated
research_questions: Does shared checked copy reduce preparation time without more factual or layout corrections?

already_counted.description: Source verification, permissions and template field capture
Copy review and final proof and provision

incremental.description: Maintain reusable templates and sample copy-source accuracy

approvals.approved_version: Exact rendered files, copy, images, dates, audience and recipient; any revision requires another proof

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=25+21+0+20=66; gross 34 minus focal upkeep 6 gives net 28 in an E1 scenario. Range 0-15 accounts for existing template automation, one-off formats and extra proofing.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Coordinate construction and removal while keeping supporting materials consistent with the exhibit.
reach: Keep event facts and permissions traceable
skills_to_grow: Review audience-specific copy and rendered proofs
role.ambitious_version: A designer who reuses checked exhibit information across useful formats while keeping live construction and removal coordination personal.
